cards.text: Jesus has been teaching in parables, like the one about a proud Pharisee and a humble tax collector (Luke 18:9-14). Now people are even bringing their babies to Him, so He can place His hands on them. BABIES, friend, and here they come!

cards.question: Jesus' disciples see people bringing their babies to Him. What do the disciples do?

cards.text: The disciples are acting like bouncers at a club: "Sorry, no babies tonight!" But Jesus calls the children to Him.

cards.question: Jesus says not to hinder the little children, because the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

cards.text: Then Jesus goes further: there's a way to receive the kingdom of God, and anyone who doesn't will NEVER enter it. Friend, I'm leaning in so close my mustache is in the dough.

cards.question: Jesus says anyone who doesn't receive the kingdom of God a certain way will never enter it. How must it be received?

cards.text: Then a certain ruler walks up to Jesus with a question, and friend, it's not "Where do I park?" It's the BIGGEST question there is.

cards.question: The ruler asks Jesus what he must do to inherit eternal ___.

cards.text: The ruler calls Jesus "Good Teacher," and out of that whole question, Jesus goes straight to one word: "Why do you call Me good?" Friend, if somebody called ME good, I'd frame it and hang it over the oven.

cards.question: Jesus tells the ruler that no one is good except God alone.

cards.text: Jesus says the ruler already knows the commandments and runs right through them: do not commit adultery, murder, steal or bear false witness, and honor your father and mother. Friend, that's the recipe card every kitchen has taped up somewhere.

cards.question: Jesus has listed the commandments. The ruler says he has kept all of them from his youth.

cards.text: From his YOUTH, friend, and I can't keep flour off my apron for five minutes! Jesus hears this and tells the ruler he still lacks one thing.

cards.question: Jesus tells the ruler to sell everything he owns and give to the ___.
Jesus says the ruler will then have treasure in heaven. After that, what does Jesus invite the ruler to do?
When the ruler hears what Jesus tells him, how does he take it?

answers.text: He runs off to sell it

cards.question: The ruler becomes very sad, because he is extremely ___.

cards.text: Jesus sees the man's sadness and says, "How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!"

cards.question: Jesus gives a picture of just how hard it is. What does He say is easier than a rich man entering the kingdom of God?

answers.text: A camel passing through the eye of a needle
A mountain being thrown into the sea
A city on a hill being hidden away

cards.text: A CAMEL, through the eye of a NEEDLE, and I can't even get my chef's hat through my own oven door without a fight! The people listening have a question of their own.

cards.question: The people who heard Jesus say this ask, "Who then can be saved?"

cards.text: Fair question! If it's that hard for the rich, they want to know who CAN make it, and Jesus has an answer.

cards.question: Jesus says what is impossible with man is possible with ___.

cards.text: Then Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, speaks up, and the first word out of his mouth is "Look," so I bet he's been holding this one in. Friend, nobody starts with "Look" to tell you the weather's nice.

cards.question: Peter tells Jesus that he and the other disciples have left all they had to ___ Jesus.

cards.text: Jesus answers, "Truly I tell you," and makes a promise to anyone who has left home or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God. Friend, when Jesus starts with "Truly I tell you," you put the mixing spoon DOWN.

cards.question: Jesus says anyone who has left home or family for the sake of the kingdom of God will receive many times more in this age.
Jesus also makes a promise about the age to come. What does He say they will receive then?

findings.problem: Calling the ruler's question the biggest question gives no basis for reasoning that "life," rather than "rest" or "glory," completes "eternal ___." The blank therefore asks for wording the baker has not seen instead of a meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The preceding setup says only that the ruler still lacks one thing. It gives no basis for choosing the poor rather than the priests or the temple as the recipients, so this blank tests unseen wording rather than an inferable meaning.
